annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence in Qatar – Principles and Guidelines for Ethical Development and Deployment
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence in Qatar – Principles and Guidelines for Ethical Development and Deployment
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (Qatar)
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Qatar's Ministry of Communications and IT issues voluntary, non-binding guidelines setting eight ethical AI principles: do no harm, robustness/security/safety, bias avoidance, environmental protection, privacy, transparency, human-centredness and human accountability. Aligned with Qatar National Vision 2030, UNESCO and OECD. Autonomous vehicles appear as a safety example.
key_provisions_or_claims: Voluntary, legally non-binding guidance updated every 1-2 years
Eight principles from 'do no harm' to ultimate human accountability
Pre-deployment risk assessment and continuous updating, referencing NCSA secure AI guidelines
Autonomous vehicles must be rigorously tested on diverse conditions such as deserts to protect pedestrians
Critical-decision AI should be regularly audited; users may challenge significant automated decisions
